issues.claim: Email/agent copy: "...ask the same safety questions your emergency page lists, and pass hazardous calls to the on-call technician without quoting prices."
issues.problem: Presupposes an on-call technician/on-call rotation exists. Nothing on the site states after-hours staffing or an on-call scheme (the audit itself asks "how nights are covered", and schema carries no opening hours), so this is an unverified presupposition sitting in client-facing copy.
issues.fix: Rephrase so it does not assert staffing: "...and route hazardous calls straight to whoever is on call." The audit body already handles this correctly by asking how nights are covered, so only the email needs the change.

issues.claim: "some reviews call pricing fair but 'a little high'"
issues.problem: The quoted fragment "a little high" is verbatim (Jim W. testimonial on /reviews/, "Price a little high but..."), but that reviewer did not call pricing "fair"; the "fair/reasonable rate... not cheap" wording is a different testimonial (Johnny D.). Merging them slightly overstates the pattern.
issues.fix: Write it as two beats: "reviews describe pricing as reasonable overall, with one calling it 'a little high'."

issues.claim: Section 2 impact range "about $1,150–$34,560 a year in gross profit"
issues.problem: Arithmetic is correct and the max/max combination is legitimate, but the top end ($34.6k) is well above the $6k–$28k range carried in analysis.json for the same opportunity, so the two documents will read inconsistently if sent together. Not a sourcing error.
issues.fix: Either reconcile the audit to analysis.json or add a half-sentence noting the top end assumes best case on all three inputs (estimate volume, recovery rate, ticket).

claims_checked.claim: Family-owned, serving New Jersey since 1989
Three offices, all sharing one phone number
24/7 emergency service advertised with a 60-minute response
Emergency page says the 60-minute time can vary (audit omits the caveat but calls it "advertised", which is accurate)
Emergency page lists the safety questions staff ask (leak location, water still flowing, shutoff closed, electrical hazard)
Page states "online scheduling is available for service requests" but directs active emergencies to call - basis for the audit's open question
Estimates are discussed on site / for most services (basis for "estimates discussed in person, with nothing visible after")
Booking or request path is a two-step form ("Step 1 of 2 · Your info", "Step 2 of 2 · Your property") with no calendar or time-slot picker; submit button reads "Request My Estimate"
No booking/scheduling page exists anywhere in the published sitemap (supports "not a pickable time slot")
Form carries an SMS consent checkbox (TCPA-style wording, STOP opt-out)
Financing exists (Synchrony application link in header and home page)
Coupons exist ($50 plumbing repair, $189 tune-up, $500 boiler, $300 HVAC, $75 sewer line, $50 water heater)
Maintenance plan promises seasonal check-ups, priority regular and emergency scheduling, and keeping equipment/serial/warranty/service records
"some reviews call pricing fair but 'a little high'"
NJ Dispatchers (43-5032) median $54,590/yr and $26.25/hr, BLS 2025 wage data
Underlying BLS API series OEUS340000000000043503213 = $54,590 (cross-check)
Assumptions behind the hours and margin figures are labelled as "our assumptions"/"our assumption" rather than presented as measured
Audit body is at most ~450 words (counted from title through the "Prepared from publicly available information" line, excluding the "For the founder" block and Sources: ~420-435 words)
Business name, town, service mix implied by the audit (plumbing, heating, AC, maintenance plans, 24/7 emergency) match the legalName and service catalogue published in the site's structured data
Walk-in opener: three offices share one number and the scheduling path is a request form
No personal data on private individuals, no reviewer names, no improper access; sources are all public business pages
